stack.choice: Node 24.22.x LTS from the official MSI, installed system-wide and hash-checked, with node -v confirmed in both Claude Code shells. Use npm with a committed lockfile and npm ci. Vite 8.3 with React ~19.3.1 and TypeScript. Set engines to >=22.12 <25 and commit .node-version. For Python, create the venv with py -3.13 -m venv .venv (the GIL build) and record python -VV.

Bare python on this machine is 3.9.13 and py defaults to 3.13t, which has no Windows wheels for numpy, shapely or rhino3dm. R3F 9.8.2 requires React below 19.4.

stack.choice: @xyflow/react 12.12.x as a view over our own store. Our own node cards carry typed handle IDs, isValidConnection, deleteKeyCode ['Delete','Backspace'], zoomOnDoubleClick false and panActivationKeyCode null. Add our own keyboard 'Connect...', an Edges list and counter-scaled 24 px port hit areas. Layout uses a topological executor with a dirty-flag cache and dagre for Tidy.

stack.licence: MIT (keep the attribution badge; removing it is a sponsorship request, not a licence term)
stack.rejected: React Flow UI Pro templates and the Pro undo/redo example (paid); vendoring React Flow UI components while their licence is UNRESOLVED; tldraw (production licence key); ComfyUI frontend (GPL-3.0); litegraph (archived); Rete.js (stale); NodePen as a dependency (prior art only)

Flagged: zundo is dormant (last release Nov 2024, last main commit Apr 2025). Vendor it, or fall back to snapshot-only undo, which is a pre-approved cut.

stack.choice: three 0.186.1 with R3F 9.8.2 and drei 10.7.9 on WebGL2, using frameloop=demand, shadows='percentage' and a flat Canvas. Effects: postprocessing 6.39 and @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 with the built-in N8AO (n8ao locked to 2.0.1, halfRes, multisampling 0), SMAA, and NEUTRAL/AGX tone mapping as the last pass. Lighting is RoomEnvironment via PMREM; HDRIs are self-hosted only. Picking and rays use three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16. Add stencil section caps.
stack.why: This is the largest ecosystem and Claude knows it well. Q03 confirmed the peer ranges against source. R3F's shadows=true selects PCFSoftShadowMap, which r186 removed, and drei Environment presets load from a third-party CDN. Flags: n8ao is CC0 on GitHub but ISC on npm; vendor performance figures are unmeasured.
stack.rejected: R3F v10 alpha (WebGPU-first); Babylon.js; xeokit (AGPL); Speckle viewer; drei Environment presets; drei Edges for massing; live drei Views for node thumbnails; CSM or SoftShadows by default

stack.choice: manifold-3d 3.5.4 in a Web Worker, in Z-up metres and local coordinates. It handles extrude with twist and taper, booleans, gross floorplate area from a mid-storey slice(), volume, sections, program tags via reserveIDs/originalID, and progress and cancel via ExecutionContext. LLM text-to-massing returns a flat JSON node list through structured outputs, and Manifold validates it.
stack.why: One small WASM package covers stacks, per-floor GFA, sections and tag tracking, and it guarantees manifold output. Q01 proposed a Python shapely/trimesh generator instead. That stays an offline and CI tool (rhino3dm .3dm export), so the browser product needs no native installs.

stack.choice: Core: the supplied Challenge site model as default context (format unknown until the brief is downloaded), .3dm via the three Rhino3dmLoader with locally hosted rhino3dm 8.35 wasm, and OBJ and glTF via three loaders. v1: IFC read through web-ifc 0.0.78 in a worker (unmodified), with an ifc-lite benchmark. The project frame stores metres, Z-up, block-centroid origin, CRS, vertical datum and northAngle, with float64 conversion at the boundary through proj4js. SketchUp and Revit come in through a documented OBJ, glTF or IFC export.
stack.why: No browser parser exists for SketchUp or Revit. Downtown streets run about 45 degrees off true north (Q03's own calculation, UNVERIFIED), so OBJ and glTF imports must ask for north before the sun module will run. Vancouver UTM coordinates break float32.
stack.licence: MIT (rhino3dm, three); MPL-2.0 (web-ifc; keep files unmodified)
stack.rejected: COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN per file; raw UTM rendering; Speckle as a core dependency; Rhino Compute as a core server; promising IFC write-back by 13 Nov

stack.choice: suncalc 2.1.1 behind one tested wrapper using real America/Vancouver instants (10:00 PDT is 17:00 UTC), plus three-mesh-bvh raycasts from grid points. The primary test is new shadow on listed parks, plazas and school sites on 22 Sep, 10:00-16:00 PDT, with existing context subtracted, a search domain of about 600 m, and the label 'draft, not a compliance determination'. The secondary metric, labelled 'course teaching metric', is Arch540 winter-solstice sun hours.
stack.why: The City's Downtown Peninsula Solar Access Guidelines (Council, 17 Sep 2025) govern a downtown block; the teaching harness does not. This overrides Q03's solstice-sized 3.3 km domain. Flagged UNVERIFIED: the guideline PDF was never opened (403), the protected-space list, time step and tolerance are team assumptions, and the suncalc check against NOAA/JPL has not been run.
stack.rejected: Solstice solar-time sun hours as the primary test; dtmass's 320 m radius and 1 m2 tolerance as fact; copying dtmass or Arch540 code without a licence; Ladybug in-process (AGPL-3.0)

Energy, wind and carbon ship as 'not modelled' cards with editable team-assumption thresholds. Ladybug runs only as an optional local plugin at arm's length. Text-extractable by-laws are sent as paragraph custom-content blocks (PDF pages only for tables and figures), and only citation JSON is committed (locator, short cited_text, URL, retrieval date). One provider-neutral evidence schema per output. OpenAI output renders as Team assumption until a source is attached. Docling handles scans in v1.

stack.choice: A 1-hour spike by 28 Oct: Cloudflare Workers static assets with _headers and SPA fallback, a separate sandbox-origin Worker, and a key-proxy Worker (run_worker_first ['/api/*'], origin allow-list, Supabase JWT verified via JWKS, AI Gateway, per-user limits in Worker code). GitHub Pages is the fallback and docs host. v1 adds Supabase (GitHub sign-in, projects, module metadata) with a keep-alive. No keys ever ship in the bundle; BYOK is opt-in and held in memory only.
stack.why: Only a header-capable host can send the CSP sandbox and COOP/COEP headers, and both vendor SDKs block browser use. Worker network wait does not count toward the 10 ms CPU limit.
stack.licence: Commercial free tiers; coi-serviceworker MIT (vendored only if needed)
stack.rejected: Cloudflare Pages (Cloudflare now steers new projects to Workers); keys in localStorage or the bundle; Render, Fly or HF Docker; Netlify

stack.choice: manifest.json (typed ports as JSON Schema, sources[], assumptions[], licence, permissions, sha256) plus a thin registry/modules.json updated by PR, with installs from tagged releases. CI checks the schema, ID uniqueness and dependency cycles (sala-tech-knowledge-tree design). Builds are deterministic and sandboxed with preview (anatomy-community pattern). giscus provides one thread per module, plus a labelling Action. From v1, third-party code runs in an opaque-origin iframe with a hardened CSP (default-src 'none', pinned script-src, img-src data: blob:, form-action and base-uri 'none') or in QuickJS. Code that touches geometry must be declarative or QuickJS.
stack.why: Moderation follows proven open patterns. A Web Worker shares the app origin and is not a sandbox, and connect-src 'none' alone still leaks data through image loads and WebRTC.
stack.licence: MIT (giscus, quickjs-emscripten); CC0 or MIT patterns only (sala has no licence, so copy its design, not its code)
stack.rejected: Plain Web Worker as a sandbox; uploads of built artefacts; installing from any git URL; star counts or trending lists

stack.choice: Boards authored in HTML/CSS with Plot SVG and a vector linework overlay (Manifold slices; three-edge-projection pinned to commit 3ac00e1 in v1). Panels export through Playwright page.screenshot as sRGB JPEG, with a quality loop that keeps each file under 10 MB and stripped metadata. page.pdf is only for course prints. AI renders use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst (edits) or -flare (drafts), pinned to the dated snapshot, take a clay+AO beauty render as reference, stay at or below 2560x1440, are upscaled locally with Real-ESRGAN (pinned by hash), and get a caption and a prompt log.

One-config provider switch (ai-agents-for-architects pattern).

instructor_tools_use.use: Adopt as the module contract, copying the patterns rather than the code (no licence): a deterministic Python evaluator is the only source of numbers, JSON in and out, a Pareto front, and UNRESOLVED after six revisions. Re-implement the gates for Windows as PreToolUse hooks in exec form (command ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.venv/Scripts/python.exe, onFailure block, Claude Code v2.1.295+). Never call python3 or use .cmd shims, use a portable lock instead of fcntl, and treat Stop-hook guards as advisory. Run the shipped demos only under WSL.

Reading list for the policy, sun, view and code modules, and the one-JSON-per-entry index format. Seed modules only from the two MIT tools (curbside, stair-core-tool). By 24 Oct, request licences from the authors of dtmass, Massing Studio and the shading tools; anything without a reply by 1 Nov is re-derived from the cited by-laws. dtmass's equinox solar code is a spec to cross-check against, not code to copy.

Optional Rhino 8 bridge for teammates, never the web import path. Ask Xun about the planned massing, structural-grid and daylighting skills before duplicating them; the facade-design recipes can feed the facade module.
Design model for module-manifest CI validation (unique IDs, prerequisite-cycle checks, verified-status field) and for spreadsheet-to-JSON bulk contribution. Copy the design, not the code.
Copy the output meta-block idea (units, sources, notes, open-sky total, formulas) and point-by-point baseline-vs-scenario comparison for every module output. Permission must come from Christina Chiu.

Link to it, without copying, as the Grasshopper onboarding path for teammates; its module-by-module tutorial structure is the model for our module cards.

Install exactly @lucasmarkes/hairline@0.5.1 (never the unscoped 'hairline'), or vendor 3-5 figures for the empty canvas, onboarding and module cards. Its ten rules (static hit areas, one accent, motion budget, reduced motion) become our linework and motion spec. Unverified: that Xun intended this repo; he only starred it.

Copy the anatomy-community submission pipeline (source-only, sandboxed deterministic rebuild, preview, per-item licence) for the module hub, and reuse anatomy's geometry-audit and headless-screenshot QA ideas. Build one capped Figure (sun path) only after 13 Nov, and drop it if it clashes with the hairline style. Never a whole tower.

Developer-only experiment for small facade or connection details after 10 Dec. Needs uv; turn telemetry off with uvx cadgen telemetry off and set CADGEN_UPDATE_CHECK=0; never disable Smart App Control. Copy its packaging pattern (skills plus local MCP) for our module-authoring skill. Not the massing node.

ux_rules: Every number on screen opens 'Why this number?' showing formula, inputs, a citation (title, link, retrieval date, section) and its status. The Vitest manifest test fails on any threshold that has neither a source nor a Team assumption flag. AI-suggested values always enter as Team assumption.

Evidence status is carried by colour, icon, word and border style together: Sourced = solid, Team assumption = dashed, FALSE ASSUMPTION = magenta hatch plus icon plus the words, also in the accessible name. A refuted claim stays visible as 'FALSE ASSUMPTION, corrected' with its history. Test: all three statuses stay distinguishable under Playwright forcedColors 'active' and in a greyscale export.

A FALSE ASSUMPTION flag on someone else's module must cite a source with a page pointer. It shows as a neutral 'Flag proposed' until a second person confirms it, the author can reply, and no points or ranks are awarded for flagging.

Each module manifest declares a cost class. Live: echo or proxy under 100 ms. Interactive: auto-run after a 300 ms debounce, with sliders evaluating on release. Batch: waits for Run and shows 'stale (upstream)' with its last result and a timestamp. A global Auto-run lock exists, and no batch module runs on project open.

Run states are always icon plus word (idle, queued, running, stale, failed, warning, done), and only 'failed' gets a hue. Over 1 s, show busy on the node; over 10 s, show percent, ETA and Cancel. No modals and no focus stealing. Errors name the cause and a fix, including the expected type on a refused wire drop.

The five-stage rail (Massing, Program, Evaluate, Design, Present) is persistent and free to jump. Each stage shows a checklist of named missing inputs, runs or sources, each linked. No percentage ring, no success colour, no reminders, and it never blocks navigation.

Every action is reachable from Ctrl/Cmd+K and from a visible Commands button. Every focused port offers a keyboard 'Connect...' listbox of type-compatible targets, and an Edges list allows delete and rewire. Single printable-key shortcuts are focus-scoped, live in one registry and can be switched off in Settings (WCAG 2.1.4).

Ports are labelled focusable buttons (for example 'Output, Shadow hours, number, h, connected to 2'). Their pointer hit areas measure at least 24 CSS px at zoom 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 in a Playwright test; below zoom 0.75, nodes switch to compact mode with a 'Connect from...' button.

Port and value popovers open on both hover and focus, close with Esc without moving focus, stay open while the pointer moves onto them, and persist until dismissed (WCAG 1.4.13). Every value shows an SI unit after a space and 3 significant figures, with full precision on hover, focus and copy.

Every analysis has a legend with units drawn from the same colour stops as the shading, a 'View as table' alternative, and one fixed scale shared across compared options. The Compare view shows up to six named snapshots with linked camera and linked inspection, each with an off switch.

A node drag, a slider scrub and an AI edit each undo as exactly one labelled step, and undo spans canvas, inspector and assumptions. Restoring a version adds a checkpoint and deletes nothing. Batch and AI runs never overwrite locked decisions (site, height band, program split) silently.

Every AI step is opt-in. It shows an estimated cost before running, labels its output 'AI draft' with model and date, offers two or more alternatives for images, and is never auto-applied to the graph. A global AI off switch exists. The sun module refuses to run until true north is confirmed for OBJ, glTF and SKP imports.

No streaks, points, leaderboards, stars, trending lists, fake urgency or nag reminders. Community listings sort by evidence completeness, then recency. Non-critical notices wait for a breakpoint (save, stage switch, run end) and never appear during a drag, wire or text edit. Screen-reader announcements are polite and batched, and only blocking failures are assertive.

Motion uses only 100, 200 or 300 ms (400 ms for large panel moves), ease-out in and ease-in out, transform and opacity only, no bounce or parallax. prefers-reduced-motion and a global 'Pause animations' switch stop edge dash animations and swap running indicators for a static icon. The canvas renders on demand and pauses offscreen.

Present mode exports each competition panel as an sRGB JPEG under 10 MB, with metadata stripped and no team, tool or platform marks. Every AI image is captioned 'AI-assisted image, model, date' and has a prompt-log entry. Effective dpi is shown, with a warning below 150 dpi. CI fails a UI PR on any serious axe violation.
visual_language: Calm 'clay and hairline'. The chrome is low-chroma neutral on a ladder of plate, hi, edge, mid, lo and accent tokens (hairline-derived, OKLCH-generated with Culori from base, accent and contrast inputs), with light, dark and high-contrast themes chosen by the user. Saturation is reserved for data and evidence. Crameri batlow is the sequential ramp and roma or vik the diverging one, only for signed deltas; analysed surfaces get a 1 px neutral edge. The evidence hues are team assumptions computed at 5.4:1 or better: Sourced blue #1D5FBF, Team assumption ochre #8A5A00, FALSE ASSUMPTION magenta #B0126F with a hatch, and failed deep red #6E0B0B. The single accent avoids all four. Typography is self-hosted Inter variable (opsz axis, tabular figures in tables and legends, five sizes) and Geist Mono for IDs, units and citations. The viewport shows matte white clay massing under a fixed RoomEnvironment rig with N8AO, NEUTRAL or AGX tone mapping and 1-1.5 px lines: darker silhouettes, lighter creases, faint context. Section, exploded-axon, analysis and diagram presets cover the rest, and every screen has one lit focal point and one next action. Motion is sparse and purposeful: 100-300 ms ease-out, one orchestrated moment, and an instant end state under reduced motion.
